text: Server-level settings apply uniformly to every database on an instance. Database-scoped configuration overrides specific settings per database, so an OLTP database and a reporting database don't have to share one setting that fits neither.

MAXDOP caps how many cores a single query can use — too high on OLTP and a few expensive queries starve everything else. Compatibility level controls which optimizer version's behavior a database uses, independent of engine version.

Azure SQL Database is already one database per logical unit, so this matters less there. Managed Instance and SQL Server on an Azure VM explicitly host multiple databases per instance — exactly what this feature was built for.

Pinning an older compatibility level buys time during a migration, but means missing every optimizer improvement since. Next up: Resource Governor, stopping one noisy workload from starving everything else.
